title: Impossibility and impracticability
summary: Impossibility and impracticability doctrines address circumstances in which an event prevents or severely disrupts the promised performance and the governing law may excuse it.
notes:
Taylor concerns destruction of the specific music hall essential to the performances. Transatlantic concerns closure of the Suez Canal when the ship could still complete the voyage by a longer route. That contrast makes the promised performance and available alternatives central. Increased cost or difficulty does not automatically establish an excuse.

Identify the event, its effect on the actual undertaking, the assumption on which the parties contracted, the allocation of risk, and any fault or contractual clause affecting the analysis. The casebook also discusses more recent disruptions as applications to test; their treatment depends on the particular contract. Keep impossibility of the performance distinct from a decline in the value the recipient expects to obtain.

textbookImport.basis: Plain-language synthesis of the cited casebook passages; subject to the jurisdictional and source limits stated there.

topics.impracticability: The analysis concerns disruption of the promised performance.
topics.risk-allocation: The contract and law determine whether that disruption excuses a party.
